questions.title: Download Cap Watch
questions.description:
A router throttles bursts: find the LONGEST run of consecutive seconds whose total traffic stays within the cap. Values are positive, so the classic sliding window works — grow the right edge, shrink the left edge whenever the sum overflows, and track the widest window. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def longest_window(nums, limit):

nums is the list of per-second traffic amounts (all positive) and limit the burst cap. Sweep with a left/right window keeping the running sum <= limit, and return the maximum window length (0 when every value alone exceeds the cap).

Input Format:
Line 1: the traffic amounts, space-separated (all positive).
Line 2: the cap.

Output Format:
One line with the longest window length.

Constraints:
1 <= len(nums) <= 1000
1 <= nums[i] <= 1000
0 <= limit <= 1000000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000; all values positive
questions.sourcecode:
def longest_window(nums, limit):
    best = 0
    total = 0
    left = 0
    for right in range(len(nums)):
        total += nums[right]
        while total > limit:
            total -= nums[left]
            left += 1
        if right - left + 1 > best:
            best = right - left + 1
    return best


def main():
    nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
    limit = int(input())
    print(longest_window(nums, limit))


main()
